links.outcome: Run-to-run repeatability (ICC) of ARCO grading across two runs by input configuration
links.effect: Mean ICC 0.51 (SD 0.18) for single image, 0.97 (SD 0.02) with description, 0.52 and 0.43 for multi-image setups; repeatability varied substantially across models and modalities in SI.
links.quote: In the SI configuration, MLLM repeatability varied substantially across models and modalities, with a mean ICC of 0.51 (SD 0.18).

links.outcome: Standalone MLLM performance versus surgeon performance under image-only input (zero-shot)
links.effect: SI input gave mean detection AUC 0.55 (SD 0.03); authors state MLLMs remain insufficient for independent diagnostic use; no with/without-AI clinician comparison.
links.quote: By contrast, the SI configuration represented zero-shot image-only interpretation and showed substantially lower performance, underscoring the current limitations of autonomous MLLM-based diagnosis.

links.outcome: Stand-alone diagnostic performance of MLLMs for ONFH detection and grading
links.effect: Single-image detection AUC 0.50-0.58 (mean 0.55); detailed ARCO grading accuracy 0.22 with SI; authors conclude none should be used independently for clinical decision-making.
links.quote: Nevertheless, none of the evaluated models should currently be used independently for clinical decision-making.

links.outcome: MLLM performance compared with surgeons and commercial versus open-source models on same data
links.effect: Surgeons mean detailed grading accuracy 0.71 (SD 0.19) versus MLLM ID ARCO 0.56; no significant commercial versus open-source difference (P=.83).
links.quote: Consistent with the bootstrap analysis, no significant overall difference was found between commercial and open-source models, though some model-specific variations existed ( Figure 5 C,D).

links.outcome: Performance of MLLMs on intended-use imaging tasks with and without radiology description
links.effect: Mean detection AUC rose from 0.55 (SD 0.03) with SI to 0.91 (SD 0.01) with ID; MI AUC mean 0.53 (SD 0.08); authors say external validation needed.
links.quote: With SI input, MLLMs showed limited diagnostic discrimination, with AUCs ranging from 0.50 to 0.58 and a mean AUC of 0.55 (SD 0.03).

links.outcome: Generalizability limits of single-center retrospective validation
links.effect: Single-center dataset only; external multicenter validation not done; authors note imaging protocol and population differences may affect performance.
links.quote: First, the single-center dataset limits generalizability.
